What we need Symbotic is seeking a Co-Op- System Engineer to join our Site Operations team within our Customer Operations organization. Your job will be to support the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of our robotic material handling system while developing hands-on experience across mechanical, electrical, robotics, and software technologies. Shadow experienced System Engineers, learn end-to-end material flow, and progressively support assigned system tickets and site activities. Analyze system alarms, performance metrics, and operational data to identify trends, recurring issues, and improvement opportunities. Document issues clearly, communicate technical concepts to site teams and customers, and partner with engineering and support teams on solutions. Assist with escalations for production-impacting problems and help coordinate follow-up actions through resolution. Follow OSHA, Symbotic, and customer safety processes and procedures while working in an active warehouse environment. Foundational knowledge of robotics, automation, electromechanical systems, controls, or industrial operations. Familiarity with one or more of the following: PLCs, SQL, Linux, Python, Power BI, Excel, data visualization, or continuous improvement practices. Hands-on interest or experience assembling, operating, testing, or troubleshooting robotics and electromechanical equipment through coursework, projects, clubs, or prior work. Ability to analyze data, organize findings, and translate observations into practical recommendations or actions. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information clearly to different audiences. Curiosity, a bias for action, and willingness to ask questions, learn unfamiliar equipment, and contribute in a fast-paced customer-site environment. Our Environment Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ. Frequent ability to safely and efficiently lift items weighing up to 60 pounds and move items weighing up to 80 pounds. Must be capable of occasional or continuous feeling, seeing, hearing, bending, twisting, stooping, pushing, pulling, balancing, gripping, climbing, crawling, sitting, handling objects, and repetitive movement using both hands and feet. Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs. System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware. System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint. System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals. Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. This role is on-site, based out of Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA. Who You Are Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog). Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical. Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs). What We Need Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications. System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware. System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs. Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis What You Will Learn Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips. Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal. Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages. Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch.
